bonuses.requirements: Evan Conrad: Most AI Startups Will Struggle to Acquire Computing PowerHomeFeedNewsEvan Conrad: Most AI Startups Will Struggle to Acquire Computing PowerEvan Conrad: Most AI Startups Will Struggle to Acquire Computing Power10/23 07:55On October 22, Evan Conrad published an article titled "The End of Startups," with the subtitle "The Coming Credit Crunch." He stated that within the next six months, most AI startups will be unable to purchase computing power, as global computing resources are sold out. To gain capacity, new cluster contracts must be signed, and it is increasingly difficult for non-investment-grade entities to secure operational capacity. Conrad noted that startups are not considered investment-grade, leading to demands for larger upfront payments. He has seen contracts requiring 100% prepayment, as lenders and cloud providers are unwilling to assume additional credit risk. He believes that investment-grade tenants are scarce, and due to leveraging and selling to non-investment-grade token buyers, their ratings have been downgraded, which he refers to as a credit bottleneck. He anticipates that investment-grade GPU buyers will increasingly require that token buyers themselves be investment-grade or make substantial upfront deposits. In his article, he provided an example where, at the time of writing, one could purchase B300 for $6 per hour and sell it for approximately $30 per hour for inference. He expects GPU prices to rise and gross margins for inference layers to decline, making it harder for lower-credit customers to obtain tokens. He proposed that lenders treat GPU clusters as collateral and mentioned that the physical delivery forward market SF Compute could allow lenders to use GPU hours on a liquidity balance sheet as collateral, rather than relying on a single service provider's cluster.BullishBearishLikeShareDisclaimer：The content above does not represent HTX's positions.，HTX does not provide any trading recommendations.。All Comments0LatestH
